taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts P. serotina and five varieties, including Texas-endemic var. eximia. The learner uses one species-level canonical entry and teaches var. eximia internally as the local Edwards Plateau concept.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — Natural Purola flora lists P. serotina as naturally occurring. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center has specimens of P. serotina var. eximia. Kerr — Kerr WMA flora lists P. serotina var. eximia.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Species-level PASS; var. eximia is taught internally and not treated as a duplicate canonical taxon.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with bark, racemes, and leaf glands. Black cherry has alternate finely serrate leaves, elongated racemes of white flowers followed by black drupes, and older bark breaking into dark scaly plates. Local Edwards Plateau plants are commonly the accepted var. eximia.
diagnostic_traits: small petiole glands near blade base
local Edwards Plateau form commonly var. eximia

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. mexicana flowers earlier in showier short clusters before leaf-out and has plum-like fruits. P. caroliniana is evergreen with glossy leaves and short axillary racemes. P. rivularis is a smaller thicket-forming plum.
